newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA SEEKS WORLD BANK SUPPORT FOR SOCIAL STEPS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA SEEKS WORLD BANK SUPPORT FOR SOCIAL STEPS.

text.p: Romania has asked for support from international lenders to cushion the effect of price hikes, the government said on Wednesday.

"We have big chances to get emergency support from the World Bank to finance social protection measures taken within the reform process we are about to start," Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea told a news conference at the end of three-day talks with World Bank representatives.

Romania's centrist government, which plans social steps to counter the effects of a recent doubling of fuel prices and and of energy price hikes expected later this month, has sought aid from international lenders including the World Bank and the European Union.

Ciorbea said his cabinet had decided to postpone the application of social protection and economic reform measures by up to three weeks in order to get vital financial support of international lenders.
He said a new accord to unlock tranches of a World Bank Financial and Enterprise Sector Adjustment Loan (FESAL) to Romania would be concluded in three weeks' time.

Last year the World Bank withheld the final tranche of about $80 million of a $280 million FESAL and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) froze three-year stand-by credits worth $460 million over slow economic reform in the Balkan country.
Romania will also start talks with the World Bank on a loan to restructure the country's agriculture, Ciorbea said.
Earlier this week, the government came under pressure from trade unions threatening to start protests over failure to balance the effect of the new fuel price rises.
Ciorbea said he was confident unionists "will understand the delay as Romania needs to get the full support of international lenders."

A team of IMF experts is expected in Bucharest on Thursday to start talks on a new memorandum in line with Romania's inflation, budget and current account deficits far beyond targets. -- Diana Voicu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3122064
